subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the approved public API be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into a broader egress policy?
rationale: The lower-level primitive exists, but exposing it changes an SSRF boundary and a public config contract that automation should not choose without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Approve Nested SSRF Policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that allows private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus metadata, redirect, cache, provider, and audit safeguards.

options.title: Keep Only Narrow Fake-IP Support
options.body: Leave current main as-is and document that arbitrary private-network `web_fetch` remains intentionally unsupported for now.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Egress Policy
options.body: Route this through the broader web-tool egress firewall design so private access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are decided together.

recommendation.title: Approve Nested SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that allows private-network access only with explicit operator intent plus metadata, redirect, cache, provider, and audit safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the clearest issue-thread guidance and has the strongest sampled history in the SSRF/guarded-fetch policy boundary.
